body:
Third spoiled gate, and a lesson about the local guard (2026-11-12, batch gate on `d7e9a807`).

What happened: with the local `reference-transaction` hook refusing moves of `main` while a gate ran, a `git pull --ff-only` still ran in the main checkout between 12:55Z and 13:00Z (right after PR #645 merged; the logs do not show who ran it). A fast-forward updates the index and the working tree first and the branch ref last, so the hook refused the ref update AFTER git had rewritten the files: the checkout was left with HEAD at `d7e9a807` and index + tree at `2b9d33e3` (16 files staged). The gate compiled the app suites across that change. The reflog shows nothing, because the ref never moved - so "check the reflog after the run" does not detect it either; `git status --short` does.

So a ref hook is the wrong guard: it turns a clean wrong-commit run into a half-moved checkout.

What is in place locally now: while a gate runs, the orchestrating session holds `.git/index.lock` in the main checkout (plus `.claude/gate-running.lock` as the readable marker). Every git command that would change the tree (pull, merge, switch, checkout, reset, stash) takes the index lock first and fails at once, before touching a file; `git fetch`, `git status`, `git rev-parse` and the linked worktrees (own index each) are unaffected, and the batch tier runs no git command that writes. Checked: `git switch --detach HEAD~1` fails with the lock present and the tree is untouched.

For the fix here:
- the gate should verify at the end that HEAD is unchanged AND `git status --short` is empty AND the tree it built is the tree at HEAD (compare `git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}` with `git write-tree` is not possible under the lock - a start/end `git status --porcelain` + `git rev-parse HEAD` pair is enough), and print VOID instead of a verdict otherwise;
- if `cargo xtask gate batch` takes the guard itself, it must also release it on every exit path (a stale `index.lock` blocks all git work in that checkout), and its message should say what the file is - git's own message tells the reader to delete it;
- the cleaner answer may be a long-lived detached gate worktree nobody pulls into, at the cost of one more `target/`.

claimed: issue-worker-medium (claude-haiku-5-5) · 2026-11-12T13:53Z · worktree/branch issue/1201-gate-checkout-moved · plan: gate detects HEAD/porcelain change in xtask (detection only, no guard), skill+AGENTS wording for worktree agents, PROCESS_VERSION 30

fix on issue/1201-gate-checkout-moved · PR #1214 · pinned by checkout_tests (head_and_tree_both_moved_say_so, half_moved_checkout_is_caught_with_head_unchanged, head_moved_with_clean_tree_names_both_commits and 3 more) · merges when reviewed. Detection only (no lock, no hook): the gate prints VOID and exits 1 when HEAD or the status moved; see docs/decisions/1201-gate-checkout-guard.md. PROCESS_VERSION 30.
